events.title: Abraham Lincoln Elected President
events.description: Republican candidate Abraham Lincoln won the United States presidential election, defeating Stephen Douglas, John C. Breckinridge, and John Bell without carrying a single Southern state.
events.significance: Lincoln's election prompted the secession of Southern states beginning with South Carolina in December 1860, leading to the American Civil War.

events.title: First Intercollegiate Football Game
events.description: Rutgers defeated Princeton 6-4 in New Brunswick, New Jersey, in what is considered the first intercollegiate American football game, played under rules closer to soccer than the modern game.
events.significance: This game marked the beginning of college football in the United States, which evolved into one of the country's most popular sports.

events.title: Birth of Adolphe Sax
events.description: Belgian instrument maker Adolphe Sax, inventor of the saxophone, was born in Dinant, Belgium.
events.significance: His invention of the saxophone in the 1840s transformed music, becoming central to jazz, classical, and popular music.

events.title: Edwin Armstrong Demonstrates FM Radio
events.description: Edwin Howard Armstrong presented his system of frequency modulation (FM) radio to the Institute of Radio Engineers in New York City.
events.significance: FM provided static-free, high-fidelity sound and became a dominant standard for radio broadcasting worldwide.

events.title: Barack Obama Re-elected President
events.description: Barack Obama won a second term as President of the United States, defeating Republican nominee Mitt Romney.
events.significance: Obama became the first Democrat since Franklin D. Roosevelt to win a majority of the popular vote in two consecutive elections.
